slides.texte_overlay:
7 money skills that'll
make you dangerously
capable in your 20s
Know your numbers. Write down what comes in, what goes out, and what's left every month. Most people in their 20s have no idea where their money goes. Ten minutes a month fixes that for good.
Build a small emergency fund first. One month of rent sitting in a separate account. When the car breaks or the job changes, you stay calm while everyone else panics and reaches for a credit card.

Learn to ask for a raise. Bring three things you did this year, with numbers. "Here's what I delivered. I'd like to talk about my salary." Most people wait to be noticed. The ones who ask usually get more.
Cancel what you don't use. Go through your subscriptions once a quarter. The gym you skip, the streaming service you forgot. It feels small, but it's often a few hundred a year just sitting there.
Understand compound interest early. Money you save at 22 has way more time to grow than money you save at 35. You don't need to be an expert. You just need to start early and stay boring about it.
Learn a little about everything. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. Knowing how the world works makes you better at money, work and people. It's the cheapest investment there is.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: twenty minutes of scrolling every morning, nothing to show for it. After: five minutes on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app, and you actually know how the world works. Same phone.

slides.texte_overlay: Never sign a loan you don't fully understand. Read the total cost, not the monthly payment. "How much will I pay in total?" is the question salesmen hope you won't ask. Ask it every single time.
